body:
for anyone else hitting this issue: there is a workaround, it's just very difficult to find. A proper fix would still be great, thank you Godot team! :-)

(from LLM below)

----

## What your bug report says

Your issue is that in the 3D editor viewport you can’t reproduce **Onshape-style navigation**: **orbit = right mouse drag** and **pan = middle mouse drag**, **both without any keyboard modifiers**. You report that the presets and “custom” options in `Editor Settings > Editors > 3D > Navigation` still force modifier combos, so you can’t get RMB-orbit + MMB-pan simultaneously. ([[GitHub](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/115776)][1])

## Workaround that usually works today: combine Navigation settings + Shortcut “modifier” entries

In current Godot 4.x, the **mouse buttons** are in `Editors > 3D > Navigation`, but the **modifier keys** are exposed as **Shortcuts** (so it’s easy to miss).

### 1) Set orbit/pan mouse buttons

Go to:

* `Editor > Editor Settings > Editors > 3D > Navigation`

  * Set **Orbit mouse button** = **Right mouse**
  * Set **Pan mouse button** = **Middle mouse**
  * Leave zoom as you prefer; **mouse wheel zoom works in all schemes**. ([[Godot Engine documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_editorsettings.html)][2])

These correspond to actual settings (`editors/3d/navigation/orbit_mouse_button` and `.../pan_mouse_button`). ([[Godot Engine documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_editorsettings.html)][2])

### 2) Remove the modifier requirement (this is the key step)

Go to:

* `Editor > Editor Settings > Shortcuts` (there’s a Shortcuts tab; Godot documents shortcut customization here). ([[Godot Engine documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/editor/default_key_mapping.html)][3])

In the search box, search for each of these and **remove all assigned keys** (so the modifier becomes effectively “None”):

* **Viewport Orbit Modifier 1**
* **Viewport Orbit Modifier 2**
* **Viewport Pan Modifier 1**
* **Viewport Pan Modifier 2**
* (Optional) **Viewport Zoom Modifier 1/2** if you also want “drag zoom” without modifiers

Those shortcut names exist in the editor (they’re present in the editor’s translation strings). ([[CoCalc](https://cocalc.com/github/godotengine/godot/blob/master/editor/translations/editor/pt.po)][4])

After this, orbit/pan should be driven only by the mouse buttons you chose in step (1), with no keyboard involvement.

## Prevent RMB-orbit from fighting Godot’s “freelook” (common gotcha)

By default, in the 3D perspective viewport, **holding RMB enters freelook**. ([[Godot Engine documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.4/tutorials/3d/introduction_to_3d.html)][5])
If you map RMB to orbit, you generally want freelook to require an extra modifier or be used via toggle.

Do this:

* `Editor > Editor Settings > Editors > 3D > Freelook`

  * Set **Freelook activation modifier** to something (e.g. **Shift** or **Ctrl**), so RMB alone won’t activate freelook. This setting explicitly exists (`editors/3d/freelook/freelook_activation_modifier`). ([[Godot Engine documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_editorsettings.html)][2])
  * You can still toggle freelook with **Shift+F** regardless. ([[Godot Engine documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_editorsettings.html)][2])

Also note (Linux): Godot warns that **Alt** can be intercepted by some window managers when clicking, so avoid building your scheme around Alt on Linux if it acts flaky. ([[Godot Engine documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_editorsettings.html)][2])

## If the UI won’t let you get “no modifiers” reliably: edit the settings file directly

Godot stores editor settings in an `editor_settings-4.tres` file (the docs even describe copying `editor_settings-3.tres` → `editor_settings-4.tres` when migrating). ([[Godot Engine documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/migrating/upgrading_to_godot_4.html)][6])
On Linux, users commonly find this under `~/.config/godot` (example given for `editor_settings-3.tres`; the 4.x filename is analogous). ([[Godot Forum](https://forum.godotengine.org/t/why-am-i-not-seeing-files-in-filesystem-tab/8398)][7])

Practical approach:

1. **Close Godot**
2. Back up `editor_settings-4.tres`
3. Re-open Godot, change *one* thing at a time in the UI (so you can see what keys/values it writes)
4. Close Godot and then edit the file to finish what the UI blocks

This is mainly useful if (for example) clearing the “Viewport … Modifier” shortcut entries doesn’t stick due to an editor bug.

## Godot extensions that help today (not exactly “Onshape mouse,” but useful)

If you’re open to add-ons that improve CAD-like navigation:

* **3Dconnexion SpaceMouse Support for Godot 4** (editor plugin + GDExtension) adds **6DoF navigation in the 3D viewport** (requires SpaceMouse hardware). ([[Godot Engine](https://godotengine.org/asset-library/asset/4646)][8])
* **Editor Camera Focus** adds a “set orbit pivot by clicking” workflow (ALT+MMB click on mesh/ground to set the orbit pivot), which many CAD/3D tools rely on for fast navigation. ([[Godot Engine](https://godotengine.org/asset-library/asset/4705)][9])

## Minimal checklist to get RMB-orbit + MMB-pan working

1. Set **Orbit mouse button = Right**, **Pan mouse button = Middle**. ([[Godot Engine documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_editorsettings.html)][2])
2. In **Shortcuts**, clear **Viewport Orbit Modifier 1/2** and **Viewport Pan Modifier 1/2**. ([[Godot Engine documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/editor/default_key_mapping.html)][3])
3. Set **Freelook activation modifier** to something so RMB alone doesn’t enter freelook. ([[Godot Engine documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_editorsettings.html)][2])

If you apply those and it still doesn’t behave (especially step 2), that’s a strong sign you’ve hit either:

* a regression/bug in shortcut removal behavior (similar to other recent viewport-modifier issues), or
* a hidden conflict in your local settings file that needs manual editing.
